required_input_schema.finite_chain_boundary: Open/periodic boundary and closing-bond convention for the displayed GAA spectrum.
required_input_schema.quasiperiodic_phase_origin: Exact site origin and phase used for the finite-chain modulation.
required_input_schema.excited_state_response: Signed/absolute denominator and degeneracy prescription for every excited-state susceptibility.
required_input_schema.finite_size_localization_rule: IPR/self-channel classification and mobility-edge rule at the plotted chain length.

T001.acceptance_boundary: Regenerate every state threshold and IPR point from the frozen GAA Hamiltonian and response convention before any source-figure comparison.
T001.acceptance_criteria: Fail closed until all finite-chain inputs that change the Fig. 2 numerical arrays are disclosed.

T002.acceptance_criteria: The AA eigensystem, scattering-channel sum, momentum observable, and literal threshold formula are finite and satisfy normalization/orthogonality invariants at reduced scale.

T003.acceptance_criteria: The reduced self-consistent branch converges with normalized states and nonnegative photon number, while the independently computed threshold landscape remains finite and positive.

required_input_schema.panel_pump_samples: Exact normal/superradiant pump value used in each of the five density panels.
required_input_schema.finite_chain_phase_origin: Exact lattice origin, quasiperiodic phase, and boundary used for the site-resolved profiles.
required_input_schema.branch_initialization: Initial orbital/field and continuation direction used to select the nonlinear branch.
required_input_schema.solver_protocol: Mixing, convergence norm, tolerance, iteration cap, and any branch-selection fallback.

T004.acceptance_boundary: Solve every density panel independently from disclosed pump and finite-chain inputs, validate normalization/convergence, then compare only as an output diagnostic.
T004.acceptance_criteria: Fail closed rather than reusing source-calibrated pump, phase, origin, or solver choices.
